hints: What is it about a word that does not change when you rearrange it? Find that, and the question becomes whether two things are equal.
How many times each letter appears is the same for every rearrangement. That tally is a canonical key: two words match exactly when their tallies match.
Count the letters of the first word into a map, then subtract the letters of the second. The words match when every count lands back on zero.
Check the lengths first - different lengths can never match, and it saves the whole tally.
